title: Vasquez: a decree to concur is understood under the condition, but God has decreed nothing about that case
source_text: V. Id observat Gabriel Vasquez in primam partem Thomae, Nihilominus, inquit, dicendum est ita Deum certo cognoscere futura sub conditione, ut etiam sub conditione subintelligatur Dei decretum de concurrendo cum arbitrio, hoc modo, Deus bene novit, si Petro in hac occasione, vel illa, darem hanc, vel illam vocationem, & ego cum illa cooperarer, secundum quod illa postularet, nec miraculose subtraherem concursum meum, fieret tale opus: possem tamen subtrahere, si placeret: utrum autem Deus esset negaturus concursum, an concessurus, in eo casu nihil decrevit ipse. Tom. 1. disput. 67. cap. 4.
pass_a_gloss: V. Gabriel Vasquez observes this on the first part of Thomas, Nevertheless, he says, it must be said that God so certainly knows futures under a condition, that under the condition there is also understood the decree of God concerning concurring with the will, in this way, God well knew, if I should give to Peter on this occasion, or that, this, or that calling, and I should cooperate with it, according as it should require, and should not miraculously withdraw my concurrence, such a work would be done: yet I could withdraw it, if it pleased me: but whether God would deny concurrence, or grant it, in that case he himself decreed nothing. Vol. 1, disputation 67, chapter 4.
pass_b_english: Gabriel Vasquez makes this point in his commentary on the first part of Thomas. 'Nevertheless,' he says, 'we must say that God knows future things under a condition with certainty in such a way that his decree to concur with the will is also understood within the condition. It runs like this. God knew well: "If on this or that occasion I gave Peter this or that call, and cooperated with it as it required, and did not miraculously withdraw my concurrence, such a deed would be done. Yet I could withdraw it if I pleased." But whether God would deny or grant his concurrence in that case, he himself decreed nothing.' Volume 1, disputation 67, chapter 4.
